tasks.short: Interview candidates with the foreman, train apprentices on the job, supervise new workers' work, fill in the apprentice's progress assessment and send it to the training centre.

steps.what: Sheet metal worker interviews candidates with the foreman
Sheet metal worker trains new employees and apprentices on the job
Sheet metal worker supervises new workers and checks the quality of their work
Sheet metal worker judges the apprentice's progress over the period
Sheet metal worker fills in the apprentice's progress assessment: on paper today; after the change the ticked skills fill it and the worker writes the comments
Sheet metal worker checks and signs the final assessment: ticked skills and comments say what the apprentice showed, for the right apprentice and training centre
Sheet metal worker sends the signed assessment to the training centre: by e-mail today, by one send from the app after the change

tasks.design: The apprentice's training plan is a checklist of work skills in the firm's work order app ({OPS_SYSTEM}); the worker ticks skills shown on real jobs, so the periodic assessment is mostly filled in. The worker writes the comments, checks and signs the assessment, and sends it to the training centre. Interviewing, training and supervising on the job stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress was written up from memory on paper forms and mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: Work order apps can hold skill checklists tied to jobs.
tasks.still_hard: Whether an apprentice is ready to work alone is a judgement, not a tick.
tasks.human_edge: Showing an apprentice how a seam should feel when it is right.

reach.learn: Whether skill checklists show gaps sooner.

evidence.claim: Work order apps can hold checklists tied to jobs.
Job logs per worker observe performance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the candidate to the assessment sent; the training centre's teaching is outside.
Input contract: training plan from the training centre; skills ticked by the worker; fallback is the paper form.
Training, supervising, judging progress and signing keep their full time. s5 keeps 60 because the ticked skills fill the form, but the worker still writes the comments. s6 keeps 20 for the send.
Checklists are used for the apprentice's learning, not to rate staff.
research_questions: Do assessments reach the training centre on time?

incremental.description: Sheet metal worker ticks skills shown on jobs.

approvals.approved_version: The progress assessment exactly as checked and signed by the worker in s5c, sent once to the apprentice's training centre; any change needs a new check and signature.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one apprentice a year with few skills ticked on jobs, so the form is mostly filled from memory (3.2); high: several apprentices with skills ticked as they go (4.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect the latest drawings, read blueprints for scope, measure on site, decide assembly sequence and methods, draw up the material list and order the materials.

steps.what: Sheet metal worker collects the latest drawings and instructions from the office
Sheet metal worker reads blueprints and drawings to determine project requirements and scope
Sheet metal worker measures on site to check the drawings against what is built
Sheet metal worker determines assembly sequences and required methods
Sheet metal worker writes the required materials list
Sheet metal worker checks the final order: articles and quantities fit the assembly plan, and the wholesaler and delivery address are right
Sheet metal worker sends the checked order to the wholesaler: by phone today, by one electronic release from the ERP after the change

tasks.design: The current drawings and instructions come with the work order on a tablet from the firm's ERP ({ERP}), so the worker does not fetch them from the office. A material list is proposed from the job calculation with article codes and prices from the sector's product data; the worker adjusts it after measuring, checks the final order and releases it to the wholesaler electronically. Reading drawings, measuring and deciding the assembly sequence stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawings were fetched on paper, and material lists handwritten and phoned in.
tasks.enabler_now: Installer ERPs send drawings to tablets and order from product data hubs.
tasks.still_hard: Site conditions often differ from the drawings.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a duct run will clash with a beam the drawing missed.

reach.learn: Whether proposed material lists need fewer changes.

evidence.claim: Syntess Atrium captures work orders, hours and materials on site and handles material ordering and call-off.
2BA is a product and price data hub that Dutch installer software connects to.

assumptions: Boundary: from the job to the order placed; delivery is outside.
Input contract: drawings from the designer via the work planner; product data from the hub; fallback is paper and phone.
Reading, measuring, deciding and the order check keep their full time. s1 keeps 30 for asking about unclear drawings. s5 keeps 40 for adjusting the proposed list. s6 keeps 20 for the release.

incremental.description: Sheet metal worker finds article codes for items missing from the product data.

approvals.approved_version: The order with articles and quantities exactly as checked by the worker in s5c, sent once electronically to the wholesaler for delivery to this job; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off jobs with many special parts, so the list is mostly written by hand (15.7); high: repeat jobs with standard materials (21.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the product specifications, look up the required sheet thickness, select gauges and types of sheet metal or other material, and check the shop's stock.

steps.what: Sheet metal worker reads the product specifications on the drawing
Sheet metal worker looks up the required sheet thickness in gauge tables
Sheet metal worker selects gauges and types of sheet metal or nonmetallic material according to product specifications
Sheet metal worker checks the shop's stock for the chosen sheet
Sheet metal worker books the sheet taken from the rack in the ERP

tasks.design: A gauge calculator in the shop's software ({OTHER}) proposes the minimum sheet thickness from duct size, pressure class and material, following the firm's duct standard. The ERP ({ERP}) shows sheet stock by thickness and type, so the worker checks the rack only to pick. Selecting the material stays with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Thickness was looked up in printed gauge tables and stock checked by walking the racks.
tasks.enabler_now: Shop software can hold gauge tables and ERP stock lists.
tasks.still_hard: Special products need a choice the tables do not cover.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a heavier sheet where a duct will take knocks.

reach.learn: Whether stock levels match the racks.

evidence.claim: Duct standards set minimum sheet thickness by duct size and pressure class, so a lookup table can propose it.

assumptions: Boundary: from the drawing to the stock check; cutting is outside.
Input contract: duct standard chosen by the firm; stock booked in the ERP; fallback is printed tables and the rack.

Reading specifications and selecting keep their full time. s2 keeps 30 for checking the proposed thickness. s4 keeps 60 for going to the rack to pick. Booking the sheet taken (s4b, share 1) is added work for the worker.

incremental.description: No further upkeep: booking sheets taken is step s4b, and the firm keeps the duct standard.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly special products outside the duct standard, so tables and racks are still checked by hand (9.4); high: mostly standard ductwork (25.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read blueprints and take dimensions, convert them into shop drawings, calculate flat patterns, check the shop drawing against the blueprint and send the cutting file to the cutter.

steps.what: Sheet metal worker reads blueprints and takes off dimensions
Sheet metal worker converts blueprints into shop drawings by hand or in 2D drawing software
Sheet metal worker calculates flat patterns for fittings
Sheet metal worker checks the shop drawing and patterns against the blueprint
Sheet metal worker sends the cutting file to the plasma cutter

tasks.design: Duct fabrication software ({OTHER}) builds shop drawings from a library of standard fittings with the worker's dimensions, and unfolds each fitting into a flat pattern in code. The worker checks the drawing and patterns against the blueprint, and only then is the nested cutting file loaded on the plasma cutter. Reading the blueprint and checking stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shop drawings and flat patterns were drawn and calculated by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Duct fabrication software unfolds standard fittings and outputs cutting files.
tasks.still_hard: Odd fittings outside the library still need hand layout.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a blueprint dimension that cannot be built as drawn.
tasks.altitude: The worker checks generated drawings instead of drawing them.

evidence.claim: Duct fabrication software unfolds standard fittings into flat patterns and outputs cutting files for plasma tables.

assumptions: Boundary: from the blueprint to the cutting job loaded; cutting and folding are outside.
Input contract: blueprints from the designer; fitting library kept by the workshop; fallback is hand layout.
Reading and checking do not change.
The cutter accepts files from the software.

incremental.description: Sheet metal worker adds new fitting types to the library.

approvals.approved_version: The nested cutting file from the shop drawing and patterns exactly as checked by the worker in s4, loaded once on the shop's plasma cutter; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many odd fittings outside the library, so most shop drawings and patterns are still made by hand (16.0); high: mostly standard ductwork (40.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The sheet metal worker keeps training apprentices, reading drawings, measuring and choosing methods and materials; fetching paper, handwritten lists, gauge tables and hand layout shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A worker who spends saved time on site quality and teaching.
